title: Does your website have to be ADA compliant?
metaDescription: Small business owners really do get demand letters over their websites. What Title III actually covers, why courts disagree, WCAG 2.1 AA, and what to fix first.

title: What privacy policy does a small business website actually need?
metaDescription: No federal law requires one. CCPA has thresholds most small shops miss. New York's SHIELD Act applies to nearly everyone. What yours needs, plus a checklist.

title: Do you need a cookie banner on your website?
metaDescription: Short answer for most US small businesses: no. But advertising pixels change that. What ePrivacy, GDPR and state privacy laws actually require, in plain English.

title: The legal basics of running an online store
metaDescription: Refund policies, FTC shipping deadlines, auto-renewals, junk fees, sales tax nexus, PCI and allergen labeling — the rules a kosher online store has to get right.

title: Email and text message marketing: the rules that actually bite
metaDescription: Email needs no opt-in. A marketing text without written consent can cost $500 a message. What CAN-SPAM and the TCPA really require before your next Yom Tov blast.

title: Building a website in Yiddish and Hebrew: what actually goes wrong
metaDescription: Why Hebrew and Yiddish sites break: mirrored layouts, prices rendering backwards, fonts with no Hebrew letters, broken search, and translation that reads wrong.

title: Delivery zones, minimums and cutoffs for a kosher grocery
metaDescription: Flat-rate delivery quietly loses money. How to draw zones by zip, set minimums and fees per zone, run cutoffs and windows, and survive the erev Yom Tov rush.

title: Running an online store that closes for Shabbos and Yom Tov
metaDescription: Why a fixed Friday 5pm cutoff is wrong most of the year, and how a frum store closes properly: real zmanim, Yom Tov, delivery dates, and automated emails.

title: Photographing food, seforim and judaica for your website
metaDescription: Bad product photos read as a store nobody trusts. How to shoot food, seforim and packaged goods with a phone, a window and $60 of gear — and size the files right.

title: WordPress or a custom-built site: which does your business need?
metaDescription: From a studio that builds both: what each really costs, where plugins bite, the middle-ground options, and five questions that settle it for your own business.

title: What should a business website actually cost?
metaDescription: Why quotes differ tenfold, real ranges for template and custom builds, the ongoing costs owners miss, and the contract clause that matters more than the price.

title: Why a slow website costs you sales
metaDescription: Your customers never tell you the page was slow, they just leave. The real causes, why images come first, and how to measure and fix your store for free.
